metadata.title: How Sttok works: shareholder register, meetings and board
metadata.description: Sttok keeps the shareholder register with numbered share ranges, runs general meetings and the board through to certified minutes, and manages incentive plans, company groups and their documents.
metadata.keywords: shareholder register, share ledger, general meeting, board of directors, company groups, beneficial owner, incentive plans

hero.title: How Sttok works: shareholder register, meetings, board, incentive plans and corporate groups
hero.description: Sttok keeps your company's corporate records: the shareholder register with numbered share ranges, general meetings and the board through to certified minutes, incentive plans and company groups. Every transaction is documented and signed in the same place.

clientsLabel: More than 250 clients keep their records in Sttok

modules.title: What Sttok does at every stage of a company's corporate life
modules.lede: Every module works on the same register. What changes in the register is reflected in the meeting, in the certificate and in the group chart.

groups.title: Shareholders and register
groups.summary: The official record of who owns what, and since when.

items.title: Official shareholder register
items.description: Register of partners or of registered shares, with share classes, numbered ranges and export in a format ready for legalisation.

items.title: Share certificate register
items.description: If the company issues share certificates, as a public limited company does, Sttok keeps their register and generates the certificates automatically with each transaction.

items.title: Transfers and encumbrances
items.description: Sales, inheritances, gifts, splits and renumbering. Pledges, usufruct, bare ownership, co-ownership and options are kept as separate positions. Every transaction opens the deed, minutes or contract behind it.

items.title: Ownership and value certificates
items.description: Issue ownership and value certificates for the company's shares automatically, for tens, hundreds or thousands of shareholders.

items.title: Onboarding from deeds
items.description: Sttok reads the deeds with AI, chains the transactions together and flags gaps in the history.

items.title: Shareholder portal
items.description: Each shareholder logs in with their email address and sees their stake in the company: shares, ranges and documents. The portal also gives access to the meetings.

items.title: Creditors and convertible notes
items.description: Each convertible note with its creditor's record, alongside the rest of the company's register.

groups.title: Governance: meetings and boards
groups.summary: Notices of general meetings and board meetings, proxies, voting, minutes and access to documents.

items.title: Shareholders' meeting
items.description: Notice sent to each shareholder, attendance list, signed proxies and live voting. The minutes are drafted from the results and sent for signature.

items.title: Board of directors
items.description: Notice with agenda, minutes and certification of resolutions.

items.title: Committees
items.description: The audit committee and the other board committees, with their members, their meetings and their minutes.

items.title: Officers and powers of attorney
items.description: Directors, administrators, attorneys and auditors with their term, the scope of each power and its registration.

items.title: Company rules
items.description: Articles of association and shareholder agreements organised by topic, with the majority each resolution requires and the calendar of obligations.

groups.title: Company groups
groups.summary: Every company in the group and who controls each one.

items.title: The whole group at a glance
items.description: Each company with its percentages, which company it depends on and its governing body. The whole group in one view.

items.title: Group chart
items.description: Subsidiaries and the chain of control on any date. A group company can be a shareholder of another.

items.title: Beneficial owner
items.description: Who holds more than 25% of the capital or the votes, or any other threshold you set, at the end of the chain, calculated from the registers.

items.title: New companies
items.description: Each company comes in with its history. If it has just been incorporated, Sttok reads the deed of incorporation.

items.title: Access control and roles
items.description: Who can enter each company and with which role. Partial access too, so other people only see the data opened to them.

items.title: Automatic documents
items.description: Sttok generates the notices, minutes and certificates of each group company from its own data.

groups.title: Transaction simulator
groups.summary: The effect of a transaction before it is signed.

items.title: Capital increases and reductions
items.description: The effect of each transaction on the actual register, including the pool and note conversion.

items.title: Sales and convertible notes
items.description: Who ends up with what percentage after each step, chaining several transactions.

items.title: Liquidation waterfall
items.description: What each shareholder receives in a sale, with the preferences of each class.

items.title: Draft documents
items.description: The simulated transaction comes with its drafts in Word for the notary or the law firm.

groups.title: Incentive plans
groups.summary: Employee and management plans, connected to the register.

items.title: Phantom shares and stock options
items.description: Each plan with its instruments, its pool and the shareholder resolution that approves it.

items.title: Vesting and grants
items.description: Sttok vests each beneficiary's units automatically, following their schedule, once they sign their invitation letter.

items.title: Beneficiary portal
items.description: Each employee sees their plan on a computer or a phone: their units, their estimated value and their vesting schedule, always up to date.

items.title: Tender offers and liquidity
items.description: Purchase windows on vested rights, with withholding and a record in the plan.

items.title: Invitation letters in bulk
items.description: From a spreadsheet of beneficiaries, Sttok generates each one's personalised letter, from one to a thousand, and sends it for signature with DocuSign. Once signed, it is filed in the beneficiary's record.

groups.title: Secondary market
groups.summary: Sales between shareholders, recorded in the register.

items.title: Sell offers
items.description: A shareholder publishes how many shares they are selling, at what price and by when.

items.title: Buy offers
items.description: The company or a shareholder makes a purchase offer to several shareholders at once.

items.title: Order book
items.description: Average price, volume and status of each offer, with its history.

items.title: Recorded in the register
items.description: Each completed transaction is entered in the shareholder register with its documents. Available as an add-on module.

groups.title: Documents, signature and communications
groups.summary: Signing, sending and generating documents, filed by company.

items.title: Built-in electronic signature
items.description: Minutes, certificates, letters and documents for shareholders are sent for signature straight from Sttok. Included in the Advanced and Pro plans.

items.title: Built-in communications
items.description: One click sends notices of general meetings and board meetings, and any other communication to shareholders, with proof of delivery.

items.title: Document generation
items.description: Notices, minutes, certificates and letters are generated automatically and filed in the company's repository.

items.title: Sttok AI
items.description: Questions in plain language about all of the company's information, and documents generated from it.

situations.title: What happens in the legal department of a company or a group, and what Sttok does

rows.situation: Year-end arrives and every subsidiary has to hold its annual general meeting
rows.action: Launches the accounts, the meetings and the filings of several companies at once, and shows on one screen what is missing in each.

rows.situation: Directors’ terms expire in several group companies
rows.action: Flags each term that expires and those still unregistered, with the file for each appointment.

rows.situation: The bank or the notary asks for a certificate of ownership
rows.action: Generates it from the register, with the company’s template or Sttok’s.

rows.situation: A buyer or an investor asks for the shareholder register in a due diligence
rows.action: Exports the register in the view they ask for, in Excel or PDF, and every transaction carries its deed, minutes or contract.

rows.situation: Compliance asks for the group’s beneficial owner
rows.action: Calculates ultimate ownership across the whole chain of companies.

rows.situation: A shareholder wants to sell their shares
rows.action: Handles the pre-emption right with its notices and deadlines, and records the transfer by ranges.
Records the inheritance, splits the numbering among the heirs and sets up co-ownership with its representative.

rows.situation: The register has to be legalised
rows.action: Prepares the register and the application, and lets you file them online or download them in Excel, CSV or PDF.

rows.situation: The external law firm needs to see only one company
rows.action: Grants access per company, also partial, so they can consult its data without entering the rest of the group.

onboarding.title: How your data gets into Sttok
paragraphs: Setting up a company takes a few hours. For groups with many companies, the time depends on the number of companies.
If the register is years out of date, Sttok rebuilds it from the deeds in a few minutes. If your data is in Excel, in another application or with your law firm, migration is part of the same process.

figures.title: Companies that already keep their records in Sttok
figures.note: More than 250 clients manage more than 500 companies. The average of two companies per client reflects the group profile of Sttok's users.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions about the product

items.a: A corporate management platform, born in Spain and also used in Portugal, Andorra and Latin America, for keeping the shareholder register, general meetings, the board of directors, incentive plans and company groups. More than 250 clients use it to manage more than 500 companies.

items.q: Does Sttok replace the shareholder register?
items.a: Sttok lets the company keep its register of partners or of registered shares by recording every transaction. It exports it in a format ready for legalisation and lets the company file it electronically with the Companies Registry when it decides to.

items.q: Can I manage every company in my group?
items.a: Yes. Each company has its own register, governing bodies and permissions, and one group company can be a shareholder of another. The chart shows the chain of control on any date.

items.q: How long does it take to get started?
items.a: A few hours per company. For groups with many companies, the time depends on the number of companies.
The secondary market is a separate add-on module. Integrated electronic signature is included in the Advanced and Pro plans.

items.q: Does it work for companies in Latin America?
items.a: The platform adapts to each country's terminology: shareholder ledger, general shareholders' meeting, board of directors. Compliance with each country's regulations is assessed case by case.
Encrypted and hosted in the European Union. Sttok is ISO 27001 certified and complies with the GDPR.
